title: Singapore Armed Forces and Other Matters Bill
what_it_is: Singapore Armed Forces and Other Matters Bill

sections.label: SAF Act amendment for DIS
sections.summary: The SAF Act was last amended in 2009, and today's amendments establish a new fourth service, the Digital and Intelligence Service.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The last time the SAF Act was amended was in 2009 to introduce the Military Domain Experts Scheme for SAF.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Nonetheless, the amendments put to this House today represent a significant change militarily to establish a new fourth service, the Digital and Intelligence Service, or DIS in short, alongside the Army, Navy and Air Force services which the SAF Act of 1972 brought into existence.

sections.label: Formal fourth service DIS
sections.summary: The amendment will set up DIS as a formal fourth service under the SAF Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Today's amendment, if approved by this House, will set up under the SAF Act a formal fourth service – DIS – and should be seen in the continuum of improvements for the SAF over the past 57 years.

sections.label: Digital domain as battle terrain
sections.summary: The digital domain has become a battle terrain that can impact a country's security and sovereignty if unguarded.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The digital domain, just like air, land and sea, has become a battle terrain which, if left unguarded, can impact the security and sovereignty of any country.

sections.label: Digital Defence sixth pillar
sections.summary: In 2019, Digital Defence was introduced as the sixth pillar of Total Defence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In 2019, we introduced Digital Defence as the sixth pillar of Total Defence.

sections.label: Dedicated service for cyber troops
sections.summary: A dedicated service is needed to raise, train and sustain cyber troops and capabilities to defend digital borders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The first response, just like the Army, Navy and Air Force, is that it will need a dedicated service to raise, train and sustain cyber troops and capabilities to defend our digital borders.

sections.label: Sections amended to include DIS
sections.summary: Sections 7(1) and 2(2)(c) are amended to include DIS as a Service under the SAF.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Sections 7(1) and 2(2)(c) are amended to include DIS as a Service under the SAF.

sections.label: Digital and Intelligence Service leadership
sections.summary: The DIS will be led by a Service Chief called the Chief of Digital and Intelligence Service, or CDI.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The DIS will be led by a Service Chief – the Chief of Digital and Intelligence Service, or CDI in short.

sections.label: CDI appointment by President
sections.summary: Section 10A of the SAF Act and Article 22(k) of the Constitution are amended to include the CDI as a presidential discretionary appointment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Section 10A of the SAF Act and Article 22(k) of the Constitution are amended to include the CDI as an appointment made by the President acting in her discretion.

sections.label: Additional limitation period start dates
sections.summary: The amendments provide for four additional dates from which the three-year limitation period starts to run.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: To provide this flexibility, the amendments provide for four additional dates from which the three-year limitation period starts to run.

sections.label: Composition fines for minor offences
sections.summary: The amendments allow composition fines up to $5,000, or half the prescribed or summary-trial maximum fine, whichever is lowest, for minor offences.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The proposed amendments allow for composition fines up to a limit of $5,000, or half of the maximum fine prescribed for the offence, or half the maximum fine that may be imposed for the offence at summary trial, whichever is lowest, to resolve minor offences efficaciously while maintaining deterrence.

sections.label: SCDF and SPF composition fines
sections.summary: The SCDF and SPF propose allowing composition of minor service or disciplinary offences with fines up to $5,000 or half the disciplinary officer's maximum fine, whichever is lower.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Similar to the SAF, the SCDF and SPF propose to allow composition of minor service or disciplinary offences, by paying a composition fine up to a cap of $5,000, or half the maximum fine that is authorised to be imposed by a disciplinary officer, whichever is lower.

sections.label: Increased maximum fines for officers and soldiers
sections.summary: For officers the maximum fine increases from $10,000 to $30,000, and for soldiers from $5,000 to $15,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: For officers, the maximum fine will increase from $10,000 to $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: For soldiers, it will increase from $5,000 to $15,000.

sections.label: Insubordinate behaviour assault imprisonment term
sections.summary: Section 19 is amended to raise the maximum imprisonment for insubordinate behaviour by assaulting a superior officer from five to seven years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Section 19 is amended to increase the maximum imprisonment term for the offence of insubordinate behaviour by assaulting a superior officer from five to seven years.

sections.label: Peacetime offence imprisonment term
sections.summary: The maximum imprisonment for the same offence committed during peacetime is increased from two to four years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The maximum imprisonment sentence for the same offence committed during peacetime will be increased from two to four years.

sections.label: SAF training in water catchment areas
sections.summary: An arrangement since the 1970s between SAF and the Public Utilities Board for military training in water catchment areas is being regularised, with the Military Manoeuvres Act amended to reflect this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Since the 1970s, there has been an arrangement between SAF and the Public Utilities Board, for the conduct of military training in certain water catchment areas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We are regularising this and the Military Manoeuvres Act is amended to reflect this.

sections.label: Fourth service Digital and Intelligence Service
sections.summary: These SAF Act amendments establish a fourth service, the Digital and Intelligence Service, following the Army, Navy and Air Force created in 1965, 1967 and 1968.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: These impressive strides were achieved because of a strong national defence and united people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: These amendments to the SAF Act to establish a fourth service – the Digital and Intelligence Service – will further strengthen our national defence, to build, for the next generation, an even better and stronger Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The creation of the armed forces for Independent Singapore started with the Singapore Army Act in December 1965.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The creation of the Singapore Navy and Air Force followed in 1967 and 1968 respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The creation of a fourth service some 54 years later is, therefore, a significant milestone.

sections.label: DIS use of C4I people
sections.summary: A question asks to what extent the DIS would be built on existing people and infrastructure in the C4I unit rather than new appointees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First, to what extent would the DIS be built on the existing people and infrastructure in the C4I unit, as opposed to new appointees?

sections.label: DIS chief civilian target question
sections.summary: A clarification asks whether the DIS chief, if in the same line as the Chiefs of the Navy, Army and Air Force, could be a target in war, and whether a civilian is intended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The one clarification I have, though, is if the DIS chief is in the same line as the Chiefs of the Navy, Army and Air Force, this actually means that that person could potentially be a target in times of war.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But if this person happens to be a civilian, then, is that really the intention of this Bill?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MINDEF plans to establish a DIS, which will be a fourth armed service, alongside the Army, Navy and Air Force.

sections.label: DIS, CSA, HTX roles
sections.summary: Asks how DIS's role differs from CSA and HTX and how they, with GovTech, share information and avoid duplication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How will the role of DIS be different from that of the Cyber Security Agency (CSA) and the Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) in countering cyber threats to Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How will these agencies, together with the Government Technology Agency (GovTech), work together, so that knowledge and information is shared, where appropriate and duplication of work is avoided?

sections.label: DIS security clearance citizenship
sections.summary: Asks whether the need for high security clearance means DIS will hire only Singapore Citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will the need for a high level of security clearance mean that DIS will hire only Singapore Citizens?

sections.label: CMPB identifying DIS talent
sections.summary: Says the Central Manpower Base should identify such talents early, before enlistment, for drafting into DIS during full-time and operationally-ready NS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Central Manpower Base should identify such talents early, even before enlistment, so that they can be drafted into the DIS during their full-time National Service and later during their Operationally-ready NS cycles.

sections.label: VEP vulnerability disclosure process
sections.summary: Says the Singapore Government should consider developing its own VEP process for deciding whether to retain or disclose vulnerabilities to vendors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Singapore Government should consider developing a VEP process of its own for determining whether to retain or disclose vulnerabilities to vendors, so that our own critical infrastructure is protected from hacking attempts.

sections.label: Commercialising MINDEF technologies framework
sections.summary: Says MINDEF should develop a framework to commercialise some technologies without compromising national security, with safeguards against abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MINDEF should develop a framework for allowing some of these technologies to be commercialised without compromising national security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This framework should also have safeguards in place to ensure that commercialised products are not abused by private organisations or foreign governments for nefarious purposes, as this could have a negative effect on Singapore's international reputation.

sections.label: Checks on DIS capabilities
sections.summary: Says DIS's technological capabilities must be balanced with checks, legal safeguards and oversight to prevent abuse of power and privacy violations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, the significant technological capabilities of the DIS must be balanced with adequate checks and balances, legal safeguards and oversight to prevent the abuse of power and violations of citizens' right to privacy, especially during peacetime.

sections.label: Vulnerability disclosure and defence tech commercialisation
sections.summary: The Government should consider a Vulnerability Equities Process, and MINDEF should develop a framework to commercialise some defence technologies without compromising national security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fourth, to safeguard Singapore's critical infrastructure from being hacked, the Government should consider implementing a Vulnerability Equities Process to decide whether to retain or disclose to vendors any vulnerabilities that its agencies, including the DIS, discover.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And fifth, MINDEF should develop a framework for allowing some defence technologies to be commercialised to benefit our nation, but without compromising national security or allowing the technologies to be abused.

sections.label: Hackers crippled satellite Internet modems
sections.summary: Reuters reported that on the day Russian forces invaded Ukraine, hackers crippled tens of thousands of satellite Internet modems in Ukraine and Europe, causing massive communications loss.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: According to a report by Reuters, the day that the Russian forces invaded Ukraine, hackers crippled tens of thousands of satellite Internet modems in Ukraine and across Europe, resulting in a massive loss in communications.

sections.label: Training cyber personnel via NSF and NSmen schemes
sections.summary: SAF intends to leverage NSFs and NSmen through expanded C4X and DCX schemes, with selected NSFs in a work-and-learn scheme with NTU earning credits toward degrees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Certainly, it takes time to train up personnel to a certain level of competency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I note that SAF intends to leverage both on NSFs, as well as our NSmen through the expansion of the Command, Control, Communications and Computers Expert (C4X) and Defence Cyber Expert (DCX) schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Selected NSFs will also undergo a work-and-learn scheme with NTU, where they can take up modules to earn academic credits, eventually, leading to a degree in data science and AI, computer science or computer engineering.

sections.label: DIS, women, and cyber precautions
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether women may voluntarily serve NS under DIS, urges personal precautions against malware and disinformation, and supports the Bill establishing DIS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I consider DIS as an invaluable opportunity for women who are keen to join the field to develop their talents and passion, as well as to reduce the gender gap in the industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Therefore, will women have the option to voluntarily serve NS under the scheme?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Every one of us has the personal responsibility to take necessary precautions against malware, and to educate ourselves against disinformation, online fraud and online security threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: These impact not just us as individuals, but also other persons and organisations that we communicate with, given the high interconnectivity of devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Special attention must also be given to the less technology-literate among us, so that they will not be left behind in our national defence against cyber attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I therefore support this Bill to establish DIS and the related constitutional amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: What is the expected proportion of uniformed and non-uniformed staff?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Will non-Singaporeans or PRs be allowed to serve in DIS?

sections.label: Summary trials and military manoeuvres in catchments
sections.summary: The speaker asks for the number of summary trials in the past five years and raises clause 37, which would let SAF carry out military manoeuvres in catchment areas with PUB approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share with the House, the number of summary trials carried out each year in the past five years?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The last point I would like to raise relates to clause 37 of the Bill which proposes to amend section 7 of the Military Manoeuvres Act to permit the SAF to carry out military manoeuvres in catchment areas with the approval of PUB.

sections.label: SAF C4I Community and Defence Cyber Organisation
sections.summary: Over the past decade, MINDEF and SAF built up the SAF C4I Community and established the Defence Cyber Organisation in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Over the past decade, MINDEF and SAF have built up what is known as the SAF C4I Community – Command, Control, Communications, Computers and Intelligence – along with the establishment of the Defence Cyber Organisation (DCO) in 2017.

sections.label: Big Tech salaries survey
sections.summary: Surveys show Big Tech firms such as Amazon Web Services, Meta, Apple and Google offer salaries up to 56.5% above the market median.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For example, surveys have surfaced that Big Tech firms, such as Amazon Web Services, Meta, Apple and Google, are dangling some of the highest salaries in the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: These salaries are pegged up to 56.5% more than the market median, according to a latest survey.

sections.label: Norway and US cyber forces
sections.summary: Examples include Norway's Cyber Defence Force, founded 2012, and the United States Cyber Command, founded 2010, and asks the intended scale of DIS manpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Examples of these include Norway's Cyber Defence Force, founded in 2012, and the United States Cyber Command, founded in 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share the intended scale of DIS in terms of manpower?

sections.label: DIS reported work scope
sections.summary: Its work will reportedly include cyber incidents response, network monitoring, vulnerability assessment and penetration testing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Its work will reportedly include cyber incidents response, network monitoring, vulnerability assessment and penetration testing.

sections.label: Compounding offences under section 79A
sections.summary: The Bill's new section 79A allows certain offences to be compounded, similar to the Criminal Procedure Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this Bill, the new section 79A allows certain offences to be compounded, similar to the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC).

sections.label: Tripling fine under section 118
sections.summary: The amended section 118 will triple the maximum amount of its fine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amended section 118 will triple the maximum amount of its fine.

sections.label: Limitation period for section 111
sections.summary: The Bill amends section 111 so the three-year limitation period, where Police investigations or civil proceedings are involved, commences only at the end of those processes or of the sentence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill amends section 111 to provide that the limitation period of three years, where there are Police investigations or civil proceedings involved, only commences at the end of those processes or of the sentence of imprisonment, detention or reformative training.

sections.label: Digital and Intelligence Service
sections.summary: The Bill will establish a Digital and Intelligence Service in the SAF to strengthen information defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This important role should not just be within the purview of MHA or MCI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Therefore, this Bill will establish a Digital and Intelligence Service in the SAF, which will play a crucial and critical role in strengthening our information defence especially in the ever-changing battlefield.

sections.label: DOTC, CCR and DIS talent
sections.summary: MINDEF announced a Digital Ops-Tech Centre and Cyber Range Centre of Excellence, and a member proposed scholarships and asked about recruiting private-sector expertise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: MINDEF has announced that it will establish a Digital Ops-Tech Centre (DOTC) and a Centre of Excellence for Cyber Range (CCR) to stimulate capability development of SAF in the digital and cyber frontier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I humbly propose that SAF can consider specific scholarships in key areas and expertise to attract, groom and train in specialised fields local talents for DIS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would SAF consider recruiting from private-sector expertise and if so, will this be on contractual basis?

sections.label: Cyber threats and DIS budget
sections.summary: Citing UK and US cyber forces, the passage says MINDEF and SAF must detect, defend, build offensive capability and allocate sufficient budget for DIS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the explainer published during the establishment of the UK National Cyber Force (NCF), part of the stated objective of the UK NCF was that it "is responsible for operating in and through cyberspace to disrupt, deny, degrade and contest those who would do harm to the UK and its allies".

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The US Army Cyber Command's mission is to "integrate and conduct cyberspace operations, electromagnetic warfare and information operations, ensuring decision dominance and freedom of action for friendly forces in and through the cyber domain and the information dimension, while denying the same to their adversaries".

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is vital that that MINDEF and SAF develop strong capabilities to detect and defend against similar threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is also critical not just to prevent such threats, but also, to build up offensive or strike capability and intelligence network, as a deterrence to those who want to do us harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There is, hence, an important need to ensure that sufficient budget and resources are allocated for our DIS of SAF in this regard.

sections.label: Online attacks before invasion
sections.summary: Disrupting electricity and communications via online attacks can weaken a nation's defence, so the speaker supports establishing the DIS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For example, by disrupting electricity and communications systems via online attacks, enemy forces can substantially weaken a nation's defence before launching a physical invasion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, I fully support the establishment of the DIS to boost our SAF's capability to defend Singapore.

sections.label: TFR and DIS recruitment
sections.summary: With a resident TFR of 1.1 below the replacement rate of 2.1, the passage asks how MINDEF will recruit and retain DIS talents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Our resident total fertility rate (TFR) of 1.1 remains substantially below the replacement rate of 2.1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this shrinking pool of human resources, how will MINDEF ensure that we will be able to recruit and retain the necessary talents to join DIS?

sections.label: 57th National Day three services
sections.summary: The passage states that next week's 57th National Day will be the last year showing capabilities of only three SAF services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In English): Madam, we celebrate our 57th National Day next week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This will be the last year where we will see demonstrations of the capabilities of only three SAF services.

sections.label: IoT vulnerabilities and ransomware increase
sections.summary: IoT numbers will double by 2025, 70% contain exploitable vulnerabilities, and ransomware rose 435% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The number of IOTs will double by 2025 to over 24 billion, of which 70% of IoTs contain vulnerabilities that can be exploited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The global risk report states a 435% increase in ransomware in 2020.

sections.label: Company paid bitcoin ransom
sections.summary: The company paid 75 bitcoin, then US$4.4 million, and received an IT tool to restore the system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Eventually, the company paid the ransom of 75 bitcoin, or US$4.4 million back then, after which, an IT tool was given to them to restore the system.

sections.label: Breach identification and containment times
sections.summary: Identifying a breach takes an average of 212 days and containing it another 75 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, it will take an average of 212 days to identify the breach and another 75 days to contain it.

sections.label: Digital and Intelligence Service addition
sections.summary: The Bill enables adding the Digital and Intelligence Service, led by the Chief of DIS reporting to the Chief of Defence Force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, I do have several clarifications to make.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This Bill will enable the addition of our fourth service – the Digital and Intelligence Service (DIS), led by the Chief of DIS, and reporting to the Chief of Defence Force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As announced in the Budget this year, DIS will be responsible for intelligence, cyber and psychological defence, as well as advancing the SAF as a networked force.

sections.label: Singapore digital jobs addition
sections.summary: A Business Times article on 7 July reported Singapore will add at least 20,000 digital jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In a recent Business Times' article on 7 July, it was reported that Singapore will add at least 20,000 digital jobs in the already heated labour market.

sections.label: SAF digital workforce manpower shortage
sections.summary: MINDEF's proposals to develop the SAF digital workforce may need effort beyond a single Ministry due to local manpower shortage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While I acknowledge MINDEF's proposal of developing our SAF digital workforce by expanding the C4X and DCX digital schemes and attracting mid-career talents, providing flexible contract options and leveraging on NSmen, this shortage of local manpower with the right skillset may require a larger effort than a single Ministry.

sections.label: Fourth service defence budget cost
sections.summary: Asks whether adding a fourth service increases defence expenditure or is contained within the current defence budget, and if additional, the expected percentage increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Will the addition of the fourth service increase our financial expenditure on defence or will the cost be contained within our current defence budget, which then implies that the other three services take a budget cut?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: If it is additional expenditure, what is the expected percentage increase in our defence budget?

sections.label: Forming Digital and Intelligence Service
sections.summary: States the fourth SAF service, the Digital and Intelligence Service, is needed to address new security threats, with DIS and CSA responsibilities delineated and digital skills upgraded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, it is important for us to form the fourth service of the SAF; that is, the Digital and Intelligence Service to address new security threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, it is important to delineate the responsibilities of the DIS and the Cyber Security Agency (CSA) to ensure that their responsibilities do not overlap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Instead, there should be inter-ministry cooperation to synergise the efforts of both organisations, in order to attain the most optimal outcome for Singapore's defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We must also look into upgrading the digital skills of our very own workforce because we cannot afford to depend on overseas talent to circumvent the shortage of manpower in Singapore itself.

sections.label: Stuxnet attack 2006
sections.summary: States that in 2006 the Stuxnet attack woke many countries up to the dangers of cyber attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In 2006, the Stuxnet attack woke many countries up to the dangers of cyber attacks.

sections.label: Saudi Aramco malware attack
sections.summary: States that in August 2012 Saudi Aramco had 30,000 of its computers demolished by malware.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Another example, in August 2012, Saudi Aramco, the world's richest company, had 30,000 of its computers demolished by malware.

sections.label: Estimated attack cost
sections.summary: States that within months analysts conservatively estimate the cost of the attack to be more than US$10 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Within months, analysts conservatively estimate that the cost of the attack to be more than US$10 billion.

sections.label: US democracy hacked 2019
sections.summary: Asks what makes Singapore think it would be spared ill intentions if the US Senate Intelligence Committee concluded in 2019 that US democracy was hacked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: If the US Senate Intelligence Committee could conclude in 2019 that US democracy was hacked, what makes us think that a small country like Singapore would be spared of ill intentions?

sections.label: DIS cyber talent salaries
sections.summary: Speaker hopes DIS benchmarks cyber talent salaries to the private sector to attract and retain staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Given that the bulk of cybersecurity expertise available to Singapore may be from the private sector, I hope that DIS can benchmark the salaries of cyber talent to the private sector, so that we can pull in the right mid-career professionals and retain good staff.

sections.label: SAF Software Bill of Materials
sections.summary: Speaker hopes DIS makes SAF mandate and implement a Software Bill of Materials policy and assess component risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Through DIS, I also hope that SAF mandate and implement a Software Bill of Materials policy, and also help SAF assess the risk of the underlying software and hardware components being deployed.

sections.label: DIS audits and CII probing
sections.summary: Speaker hopes DIS audits people, processes and tools, works with CSA, and probes Critical Information Infrastructure for vulnerabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: DIS needs an extremely vigorous process to audit our people and processes, and the security of our tools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Last of all, I hope that DIS will work hand in glove with our Cybersecurity Agency of Singapore (CSA) to protect Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I hope DIS can actively contribute by to our Critical Information Infrastructure (CII) by probing our CIIs for vulnerabilities.

sections.label: SAF transition and DIS setup
sections.summary: SAF is transitioning to a fourth generation army, and the proposed Digital and Intelligence Services boosts its cyber and digital defence capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To tackle the multitude of new security threats, SAF has begun its transition from a third generation army to a fourth generation one, fortifying its capabilities to confront more complex defence challenges with more modern technologies and newer equipment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am, thus, happy to learn that SAF has continued its earlier trajectory of boosting its cyber and digital defence capabilities with the proposed setting up of the Digital and Intelligence Services (DIS).

sections.label: DIS jurisdiction boundaries
sections.summary: Speaker asks where DIS jurisdiction begins and ends, especially for national-level cybersecurity matters and threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While I agree wholeheartedly with the setting up of DIS, I would like to ask where does the jurisdiction of DIS begins and where does it end, especially regarding cybersecurity matters and threats that could have an impact at the national level?

sections.label: Military Manoeuvres Act amendments
sections.summary: The Bill amends the Military Manoeuvres Act of 1905 to let SAF carry out manoeuvres in catchment areas with PUB approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The second part of the Bill proposes amendments to the Military Manoeuvres Act of 1905 to permit the SAF to carry out of military manoeuvres in catchment areas with the approval of the Public Utilities Board.

sections.label: Military exercises environmental impact study
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked whether it plans an environmental impact study or engagement with agencies and nature groups on military exercises' impact on catchment areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Does MINDEF plan to do any environmental impact study or engage the relevant agencies and perhaps even nature groups with regards to the impact of such military exercises on the catchment areas, so we can minimise the ecological footprints of such activities on our natural environment?

sections.label: Constitution Amendment Bill and DIS Chief
sections.summary: The Constitution (Amendment) Bill adds the Chief of the DIS to key public sector appointments requiring the President's agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My speech is restricted to the Constitution (Amendment) Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This Bill enjoins the Chief of the DIS to the list of key public sector appointments that must be agreed to, by the President.

sections.label: Workers' Party voting on Bills
sections.summary: The Workers' Party will vote against the Constitution (Amendment) Bill, support the Singapore Armed Forces and Other Matters Bill, but not clause 6.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In view of the Workers' Party's position on the elected presidency, we will vote against the Constitution (Amendment) Bill as a matter of principle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For the Singapore Armed Forces and Other Matters Bill, we will support the Bill, but cannot support clause 6, which is specifically related to the President's discretionary powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, since the substantive change is located in the Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (Amendment) Bill, we will support the Singapore Armed Forces and Other Matters Bill as our position is clarified by voting against the constitutional amendment.

sections.label: SAF missions against digital threats
sections.summary: There was unanimous agreement that SAF's missions must also protect Singapore against digital threats, as in air, land and sea.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But in the interest of disclosure and to make sure that we do not perpetuate scams, if you do get one after this, please know it is not from me and do not answer it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: There has been unanimous agreement that, just as we do in the air, land and sea, SAF's missions must also protect Singapore against digital threats.

sections.label: Reasons for decision
sections.summary: Two main reasons led to this decision: manpower and mission mindset.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: At the end of it, two main reasons led to this decision – manpower and mission mindset.

sections.label: Formal fourth service for DIS
sections.summary: Forming a formal fourth service on par with the Army, Navy and Air Force is the best footing for DIS to attract the right people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Forming a formal fourth service on par with the Army, Navy and Air Force is the best footing for DIS to attract the right type of people it needs.

sections.label: C4I and cyber domain protection
sections.summary: The C4I community continues supporting other domains, and with the DIS as a formal service it is directly responsible and accountable for protecting the cyber domain against external aggressors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The C4I community will continue to perform these supporting roles for other domains.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But with the DIS as a formal service, it is now also directly responsible and accountable to protect the cyber domain against external aggressors.

sections.label: Cyber NSF Scheme and DIS sizing
sections.summary: The Cyber NSF Scheme trains NSFs in threat monitoring and assessment, with selected ones becoming cyber specialists, and the DIS will grow organically to two or three times the MIO.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The Cyber NSF Scheme, which Members alluded to, provides training in threat monitoring and assessment for NSFs to become cyber operators during their two-year full-time National Service.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Selected ones with leadership aptitude may be selected to become cyber specialists in a three-year or four-year undergraduate work-learn programme where they will perform specialised roles, such as incident response, cyber forensic, malware analysis and penetration testing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Members have asked about the sizing of the DIS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I mentioned before in this House that it will grow organically from the current MIO and, at steady state, I think it will likely be two or three times that.

sections.label: DIS and cyber ranges
sections.summary: When the new service DIS is formed, it can help build more sophisticated cyber ranges that add depth and realism for exercises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: When the new service, DIS, is formed, it can help build more sophisticated cyber ranges that can add depth and realism for these exercises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I have already announced the setting up of a new Digital Ops-Tech Centre and a state-of-the-art digital training and simulation range.

sections.label: Composition for abetment of lesser offences
sections.summary: For the abetment of lesser offences, MINDEF is open to allowing composition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: For the abetment of lesser offences, I think this was mentioned by Mr Dennis Tan as well, MINDEF is open to allowing composition.

sections.label: No charge for authorised composition
sections.summary: In all cases referred to an authorised composition officer, no charge is preferred.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In all cases referred to an authorised composition officer, no charge is preferred.

sections.label: Chief Military Prosecutor jurisdiction
sections.summary: For military offences, the Chief Military Prosecutor ensures compounded offences are broadly aligned to the civil justice system while considering military discipline.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: For military offences, the jurisdiction comes under the Chief Military Prosecutor who will ensure that compounded offences are broadly aligned to the civil justice system but take into account the need for military discipline.

sections.label: DIS and cyber threats
sections.summary: The DIS positions the SAF and Singapore to better deal with cyber threats now and in the future.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The DIS positions the SAF and Singapore to better deal with cyber threats today and into the future.

sections.label: DIS competition not a signal
sections.summary: Saying the DIS should compete with other services is not a signal to "chiong".

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: When I said that the formation of the fourth service, the DIS, should compete with the other services, it is not a signal to "chiong".

sections.label: DIS competition and talent shortage
sections.summary: The DIS is on a more equal footing but must compete, and talent is acutely short, so the overall pie must grow or efficiency found, working with other agencies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And with the formation of the DIS, it puts it on a somewhat more equal footing, but they will have to compete.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But I agree completely with Mr Giam and, I think, others spoke about it, that we are acutely short of these talents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We will have to grow the overall pie or find ways of being efficient.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And I completely agree and, yes, the answer is that we will work with other agencies.
